content.text:
**The original problem**

You decided that JusPrin never asks a person to save or discard. Autosave keeps the work, and version history is how you get it back. Then this case came up. A person has edited their printer's settings in the open project without saving them, and then tells the printer chat "I put a 0.6 nozzle on it." Changing the nozzle replaces the project's copy of the printer settings, which would throw those unsaved edits away.

The fix made on 2026-10-14 says the nozzle may change only after those edits are saved into the project's version history. If that save fails, the nozzle stays as it was, and the chat's AI gets an error saying the edits couldn't be saved. You said this was wrong too, without saying what's right. Nobody had decided what the AI should say or do after that error, so it was left to improvise. My job was to work out the right behaviour.

**What I found when I tested it**

The error everyone was worried about almost never reaches anyone. Before the printer chat changes the nozzle, it already saves a version of the project, the same way the main AI chat does before any change. If that save fails, the whole request stops there with a general "Couldn't save the project, nothing was changed" error. The more specific "unsaved edits couldn't be saved" check runs a moment later, right after a save that just succeeded, so it practically never fails. The case to design for is the general save failure, not the specific one.

**The other problems I ran into**

1. **A successful change is reported as a failure.** This is the serious one. The printer chat numbers its actions starting from 1 every time it opens, but it files them in the project's permanent history. So the second time someone opens the printer chat and changes something on the same project, the number is already taken. The change goes through, but the AI is told it failed, and it tells the person so. I reproduced this in the test harness. It also affects settings changes made in the printer and filament chats, and it's probably the most likely error a real person sees today. A separate session is already fixing it.

2. **A save problem blocks changes that don't touch the project.** If the project can't be saved, the person also can't change the nozzle on a different printer that this project doesn't use. That change wouldn't affect the project at all, so there's no reason to block it.

3. **The real reason is thrown away.** When a save fails, the app knows why, for example "permission denied", a full disk, or a paint tool still open in the 3D view. That reason goes only to the log. The AI just hears "couldn't save", so it can't tell the person what to do.

4. **The AI's likely improvisation leads back to a save-or-discard prompt.** The printer chat shows no card for a nozzle change, so the person only sees what the AI writes. The AI's instructions say nothing about this error. A natural thing for it to say is "you can change the nozzle yourself in printer settings." But if the person switches printer profiles by hand, OrcaSlicer's own "save or discard your changes?" dialog still appears. That's exactly the prompt you ruled out. I haven't seen the AI actually say this, because checking would need a live run you haven't approved.

**What I propose**

First, fix the numbering bug, because it gives people false failures right now.

Second, stop throwing away the unsaved edits when the nozzle changes. Keep them, still unsaved, the way renaming a printer and connecting a printer already do. The only settings the new nozzle replaces are the nine where the 0.4 and 0.6 nozzle profiles actually differ, such as nozzle diameter, layer-height limits, retraction and the start G-code. The printer's saved settings already follow that rule. The nozzle change then stops depending on a special extra save, and only one simple rule is left: if the project can't be saved first, nothing changes.

Third, don't require a project save when the project doesn't use the printer being changed.

Fourth, when a save does fail, have the error itself say why in plain words and what to do next, such as "close the paint tool and ask again." The AI can then pass that on without needing a special instruction.

I would not retry automatically. The app already retries saving every two seconds on its own, and the real causes don't fix themselves within a second. Running the nozzle change later, once saving works, would change the printer after the person may have left the chat.

I also drafted one sentence for the AI's instructions: "If the project can't be saved, say nothing changed and why, and never suggest doing it another way in the app." I'd only add it if a live test you approve shows the AI still improvising. Another task is currently rewriting those instructions, so it would need to go through them.

content.text:
Here are the failure cases that could plausibly happen to a real person, most likely first. I've dropped the ones I created by making storage refuse writes, and the "unsaved edits couldn't be saved" check failing on its own, which practically can't happen.

1. **The person changes something in the printer chat a second time on the same project.** For example, they set the nozzle to 0.6 today and switch it back to 0.4 tomorrow. The change goes through, but the AI is told it failed and says so. I reproduced this in the test harness. It comes from the printer chat restarting its action numbering every time it opens. The separate session you started is fixing it.

2. **A paint, seam, support or cut tool is open in the 3D view, with work not yet saved, when the person asks for a nozzle change.** Autosave deliberately waits while one of those tools is open. So the save the printer chat makes before every change fails, and nothing changes. This happens even if the person has no unsaved printer edits. The error the app produces says "Finish the current tool edit before replacing the project," which is the wrong wording here, and the AI only hears "Couldn't save the project." I found this by reading the code and haven't reproduced it. I also haven't checked whether the printer chat can be opened while one of those tools is open.

3. **Right after JusPrin starts, before the 3D view has ever been drawn.** For example, the app opens on Home and the person goes straight to the printer chat to change the nozzle. If the project has anything not yet saved, the save fails with "The project canvas is not ready," and nothing changes. This is also from reading the code and not reproduced. I don't know yet whether the 3D view gets drawn behind Home at startup. If it does, this case can't happen.

4. **The disk is full.** The save fails and nothing changes. The header already shows "Couldn't save," but the AI isn't told why, so it can't tell the person to free up space. This one is rare but real.

5. **Possibly: a second copy of JusPrin has the same project open.** Each project is locked to the copy that opened it. I haven't checked what the second copy does when it tries to save, so this may not be a real case.

For cases 2 to 5 there's a knock-on effect: while saving is broken, the person also can't change the nozzle on a printer the open project doesn't even use.

I'd reproduce 2 and 3 next in the test harness. They are the likeliest real failures after the numbering bug, and each one depends on a fact I haven't checked yet.

11	Found 2026-10-14 on `claude/no-save-prompts`. Ever since 7852470aff installed the shell's version callbacks on the printer panel, each panel opening has used a fresh in-memory ProjectPersistence, so its action ids restart at "t-1". ProjectVersionStore::record_operation then refuses the duplicate operations/t-1.json. A second versioned call (printer_change, settings_apply_patch) from a later opening on the same project goes through, but it reports local_save_failed "The action ran, but its changes couldn't be saved". A fix task chip was offered, but it was not fixed then.
12	
13	**Why:** a false failure is the most likely thing a person sees after a panel change, and it looks like a save problem, not an id problem.
14	
15	**How to apply:** when a panel tool reports local_save_failed with autosave state Saved, look for "operation version record already exists" in the log before blaming storage. Check whether this is fixed (grep PrinterPanel build_runtime for the id allocator) before trusting this note. The nozzle-change proposal is the untracked file nozzle-change-failed-proposal.md in worktree bold-cohen-1cf36c. Related: [[tool-call-approval-removed]], [[autosave-design-research]].

commit 336facf825305eab9876e21719d98b0081d4ce23
Author: Kenneth Jiang <kenneth.jiang@gmail.com>
Date:   Wed Oct 14 18:02:11 2026 -0700

    No save-or-discard prompts; ask only about files opened before
    
    On 2026-09-29 Kenneth decided JusPrin never asks a person to save or
    discard: autosave keeps the work and version history is the way back.
    Several paths still refused or asked. This brings them in line, and makes
    the one question that remains, about a file opened before, consistent.
    
    Save or discard:
    - project_open releases the project through new_project, whose autosave
      hook saves it first; a failed save is the tool error. unsavedWork and the
      refusal are gone. Edited presets are dropped after the save.
    - printer_setup drops unsaved preset edits and lists them in discarded;
      unsavedEdits and its refusal are gone.
    - Saving another filament drops the open filament's unsaved edits and
      warns discards_unsaved_edits instead of refusing.
    - Plater::load_project no longer stops opening a file over unsaved changes.
      That check fired even with autosave running, because autosave never
      resets Orca's own save tracker. Its prompt-table row is gone.
    - A printer's nozzle change on the project's printer changes only after
      the unsaved edits are saved to version history; otherwise nothing
      changes. The printer panel's agent saves a version before printer_change,
      which lists the dropped keys in discarded.
    - Connecting a printer keeps the project's other unsaved edits; renaming a
      printer no longer raises Orca's prompt and keeps the edits unsaved.
    
    Skipped confirmations:

lines: -# When a nozzle change can't keep the printer's unsaved edits
-Written 2026-10-14 for Kenneth. Based on `claude/no-save-prompts` (7852470aff, d33fb306c9). Nothing committed or pushed.

-You tell the printer panel "I put a 0.6 nozzle on it" while the open project uses that printer and has unsaved edits to it. Before `printer_change` runs, the panel saves a version of the project, as the agent pane does for every change. If that save fails, the call fails with `local_save_failed`, "Couldn't save the project. The action was not run.", and nothing changes. The real reason (in the harness, "Permission denied") goes only to the log.

-So the `change_failed` message about history is practically unreachable through the panel. By the time the nozzle code asks for the edits to be saved, a version was saved a moment earlier. Only the harness reaches it, by calling the backend directly.
-The model gets nothing else. The panel draws no card for `printer_change`. The prompt has no rule for either error. The header shows "Couldn't save" and retries by itself.
-Measured with `JusPrinShellHarness --printer-setup` and a temporary probe that makes the project's storage refuse writes. All existing nozzle checks pass.
-| Case | What the model reads | What happened |
-| Project's printer, unsaved edit, storage refuses | `local_save_failed` | Nothing changed (correct) |
-| A printer the project does not use, storage refuses | `local_save_failed` | Refused, though the project would not change |
-| Same call after storage recovers | `local_save_failed`, "The action ran, but its changes couldn't be saved" | **The nozzle changed and the edit was dropped** |

-The last row is a separate bug. The panel numbers its actions from `t-1` each time it opens, but files them in the project's permanent history. The second versioned call from any later panel opening on the same project collides ("operation version record already exists"). The model then says the change failed when it happened. This affects settings applies in the panel too. Today, this false failure is the one people are most likely to see.

-1. **Retry automatically.** Autosave already retries every 2 seconds. Retrying inside the call doesn't help the real causes: storage refusing writes, a full disk, or a paint or cut tool open in the 3D editor. Running the change later, once saving works, would change the printer after the person may have left. Not recommended.

-2. **Keep the unsaved edits across the change, as renaming and connecting already do.** Only the 9 settings the 0.4 and 0.6 profiles disagree on are replaced: `nozzle_diameter`, `max_layer_height`, `min_layer_height`, `retraction_length`, `retraction_minimum_travel`, `machine_start_gcode`, `printer_variant`, `default_print_profile`, `upward_compatible_machine`. The printer's saved changes already follow this rule. The extra save step and its message go away, so one rule is left: no saved version, no change.
-3. **Don't require a project save when the project doesn't use the printer.**
-4. **Make the error say why and what next**, in plain words: "the project's storage refused the write", "finish the paint tool first", then "ask again once the header no longer says Couldn't save".

-5. **One sentence of prompt guidance**: "If a tool fails with local_save_failed, nothing changed: say why in one sentence and that they can ask again once the project saves; never suggest making the change another way in the app." The last part matters because Orca's save-or-discard dialog still opens when a person switches printer profiles by hand. I have not checked whether the model actually suggests that; it would need a live run.

-First, fix the id collision; it gives false failures today. Then do 2, 3 and 4. With those, the failure is rare, nothing is lost, and the error itself tells the model what to say. Add 5 only if a live batch you approve shows the model still improvising. That sentence also belongs to whoever is restructuring `printerInstructions.ts`.

content.text:
I removed the special save step from the nozzle change. Any failure to save the project now goes through the same generic error as every other change, and the person isn't shown a popup. If the save before a nozzle change fails, the nozzle stays as it was and the person's unsaved printer edits are untouched. The AI gets the usual "Couldn't save the project. The action was not run." and the header shows "Couldn't save". Nothing is committed yet.

**What changed** (11 files, 43 lines added, 50 removed):
- The nozzle change no longer runs its own save of the unsaved edits, and its special message is gone: "The unsaved changes to this printer couldn't be saved to the project's history…". The save the printer chat makes before every change already puts those edits in version history, so the extra step only ever duplicated it.
- The step's plumbing through the printer chat, the printer backend and the shell is removed.
- The tool description, the code comment and the printer chat section of the tool guide now say where the protection lives: the save before the change. If that save fails, nothing runs and the generic error is returned.
- In the test harness, the two checks for the removed step are replaced by one check. It makes a nozzle change through the real printer chat while the project can't be saved, and expects the generic error, the nozzle unchanged and the unsaved edit still there.

**Testing:**
- Printer-setup harness: 201 checks pass.
- Default harness: 553 checks pass.
- Agent tests: 277 pass.
- To make sure the new check would catch a regression, I temporarily turned off the save before the change. The new check failed, and so did the existing check that restores the dropped edit from history. Then I put the code back.

**Things you should know:**
- `claude/no-save-prompts` was squashed into one commit, 336facf825, while I was working. I moved my change onto that commit, and it applied cleanly. The squash's commit message still says the nozzle changes "only after the unsaved edits are saved to version history". That's still true in effect, but the save now happens in the step before the change.
- The session fixing the action-numbering bug touches the same printer chat code, the shell setup code and the harness. Whichever lands second will probably have a small merge conflict.

The work is uncommitted on `claude/nozzle-change-failed` in my worktree. Do you want me to commit it?
